standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness over a valuation ring is the same as torsion freeness
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the author remove torsion parts, which is the key reduction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homogenisation: a finite type algebra over a ring is the degree zero part of a graded algebra generated in degree one, and similarly for modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-homogenize}, cited at proof lines 5983-5988
standard_prerequisites.use: Realises the algebra and the module as localisations of graded objects.

standard_prerequisites.name: The torsion submodule can be removed without changing the degree zero part of a graded module
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes both the graded algebra and the graded module torsion free.

standard_prerequisites.name: A flat graded algebra of finite type over a local ring and a flat finite graded module over it are finitely presented
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation} and Lemma \ref{lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation-module}, cited at proof lines 5994-5996 and 5999-6001
standard_prerequisites.use: Give the two graded statements which specialise to the required results.

core_obligations: Recall the equivalence of flatness and torsion freeness over a valuation ring (proof lines 5981-5982).
Homogenise the algebra and the module, and remove torsion parts so that both are torsion free (proof lines 5983-5992).
Apply the graded algebra statement to get finite presentation in the first case (proof lines 5993-5997).
Replace the graded algebra by a graded polynomial ring and apply the graded module statement for the second case (proof lines 5998-6002).
proof_roadmap: Case (1) by the graded algebra statement (proof lines 5993-5997).
Case (2) by the graded module statement (proof lines 5998-6002).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that over a valuation ring a flat algebra of finite type is finitely presented and a finite module which is flat over the ring is finitely presented over its algebra. The statement carries a literature reference; the text gives its own proof, which uses the equivalence between flatness and torsion freeness over a valuation ring to homogenise the situation: the algebra and the module are realised as the degree zero parts of a graded algebra of finite type over the ring and a finite graded module over it, torsion parts are removed so that the relevant objects are torsion free, and the corresponding statements for graded algebras and graded modules over a local ring are then applied.
